title: The Llama's Bakery
text: Lulu the llama opened a bakery before sunrise. She made round rolls, square pies, and one cookie shaped like a sock. The cookie won first prize. No one ate it, because everyone wanted to wear it on a cold foot.
context: An original silly story about an unusual baker.
vocabulary: bakery: a place that makes and sells baked food

title: The Moon Misses the Bus
text: The moon missed the night bus and had to roll home. It rolled over a hill, around a pond, and past a sleepy cow. By sunrise, the moon reached the sky. “Next time,” it puffed, “I will leave early.”
context: An original make-believe story about the moon traveling home.
vocabulary: sunrise: the time when the sun appears

title: The Robot's Sandwich Garden
text: Rex the robot planted three sandwich seeds. He watered them with tomato soup. Soon, tiny cheese leaves popped from the dirt. Rex picked one sandwich for lunch. It tasted like mud, so he planted a spoon tree instead.
context: An original silly story about a robot gardener.
vocabulary: planted: put seeds in the ground

title: The Invisible Purple Hat
text: Nina wore an invisible purple hat to school. No one could see it, but everyone agreed it looked wonderful. At recess, a gust of wind blew the hat away. The class searched everywhere. They found it exactly where nobody was looking.
context: An original story about a hat that cannot be seen.
vocabulary: gust: a short burst of wind

title: The Dragon Who Could Not Sneeze
text: A dragon felt a sneeze tickle his nose. He sniffed pepper, feathers, and a dusty rug. Nothing worked. Then a butterfly landed on his nose. “Ah-choo!” The sneeze toasted six marshmallows, and the butterfly asked for another turn.
context: An original gentle dragon story with a warm ending.

title: The Pirate and the Puddle
text: Captain Bea sailed across a giant puddle in a paper boat. She passed a floating leaf and waved to a brave ant. Then her ship bumped the curb. Bea raised her spoon and cried, “Land!” The voyage had lasted four minutes.
vocabulary: voyage: a long trip, often by water
curb: the raised edge of a street

title: A Cloud in My Backpack
text: Sam found a small cloud hiding in his backpack. It rained on his pencils and snowed on his lunch. Sam opened the zipper and pointed outside. The cloud floated away, but it left one tiny rainbow curled around an eraser.
context: An original school story about pocket-sized weather.
vocabulary: floated: moved gently through the air

title: Grandma's Racing Teapot
text: Grandma's teapot grew wheels on Tuesday. It raced the sugar bowl around the kitchen and won by one spoon. Grandma gave it a shiny ribbon. The teapot whistled proudly, then parked beside the cups and took a quiet nap.
context: An original kitchen race with friendly objects.
vocabulary: ribbon: a narrow strip of cloth used as a prize

title: The Sock Who Became Mayor
text: A blue sock became mayor of the laundry basket. Its first rule was simple: every sock needed a partner. The lonely socks cheered. By Friday, they had formed pairs, except for one green sock that happily wore a mitten.
objectives: find the story problem and solution
context: An original story about teamwork in a laundry basket.
vocabulary: mayor: the leader of a town or city

title: The Pancake Learns to Fly
text: A pancake jumped from the pan and tried to fly. It flapped two pats of butter like wings. Up it rose, past the table and over a chair. Then syrup made it sticky, so it landed safely on a hungry plate.
context: An original breakfast story with a flying pancake.
vocabulary: flapped: moved up and down like wings

title: The Backpack That Hiccupped
text: Maya's backpack hiccupped during math. Out popped a pencil, a sock, and yesterday's banana. “Excuse me,” whispered Maya. The backpack hiccupped again and launched her homework onto the teacher's desk. At least the work arrived on time, even if the banana did not.
context: An original school story about a noisy backpack.
vocabulary: launched: sent quickly through the air

title: The Banana Detective
text: Detective Banana found yellow footprints across the kitchen. He followed them past the sink and under the table. The trail ended at a fruit bowl. “Aha!” he cried. Then he looked down. The footprints were his own. He peeled away from the case very quietly.
context: An original mystery starring a confused banana.
vocabulary: detective: a person who solves mysteries

title: Tuesday Turns Purple
text: On Tuesday, everything turned purple. The toast was purple. The school bus was purple. Even Mr. Lee's white shoes looked like grapes. On Wednesday, every color returned except one. The class hamster stayed purple and seemed very pleased about it.
context: An original color-changing story with a hamster ending.

title: The Hamster's Tiny Elevator
text: Pip built an elevator for his hamster. It went from the floor to the top of the couch. The hamster rode up, ate one cracker, and pushed the button again. Soon it was giving rides to three buttons, a marble, and a sleepy beetle.
context: An original story about a very small elevator.
vocabulary: elevator: a platform that carries things up or down

title: The Shoes Take a Walk
text: Leo's shoes went for a walk without him. They marched down the hall, skipped over a rug, and waited by the door. “You forgot something,” Leo called. The shoes looked back. Of course! They returned, picked up Leo, and carried him to breakfast.
context: An original morning story about independent shoes.
vocabulary: marched: walked with steady, even steps
